review_candidates.description: The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work http//www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Program And Position Overview While Malawi has made important advances in improving maternal and newborn health (MNH) outcomes, this progress has stagnated since 2019. High rates of maternal mortality (224 per 100,000 live births) and neonatal mortality (24 per 1,000 live births) point to major gaps in the quality of care.* Malawi's health system faces numerous challenges in delivering high-quality MNH services, including inadequate facilities, insufficient medical equipment and commodities, and a shortage of qualified health workers both in terms of numbers and skill-mix. To address these challenges, CHAI is working with the Government of Malawi and a consortium of partners to develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate a robust Country Investment Plan for strengthening MNH services and improving MNH outcomes. The MNH Investment Plan will focus on operationalizing priority interventions during antenatal care, labour and delivery, and newborn care targeted at the primary drivers of maternal and neonatal mortality and stillbirths. Under this program, CHAI staff will work closely with the Ministry of Health to implement evidence-based strategies that will improve the availability of quality MNH commodities; increase the number, competency, and skill-mix of the MNH workforce; reinforce MNH data in national health information systems; support maternity and neonatal unit infrastructure development; and strengthen referrals and emergency transport for obstetric and newborn emergencies. CHAI Malawi seeks Supply Chain Associate, who will be based in Lilongwe, and seconded to the Ministry of Health, Reproductive Health Directorate. The Supply Chain Associate will report directly to the Director Reproductive Health Directorate. For administrative and contracting issues, the role will report to the Program Manager, Sexual Reproductive Maternal and Newborn Health (SRMNH) at CHAI. This is a challenging but rewarding position which will directly impact the government’s capacity to deliver improved health services for the country’s population. It presents an opportunity to work closely with a government that is committed to finding opportunities for bolstering the national and subnational delivery of Reproductive Health (RH) services and delivering a stronger health system for the people of Malawi. National Statistical Office (NSO), Utica International, and ICF. 2025. Malawi Demographic and Health Survey 2024 Final Report. Support MoH, in routine supply chain monitoring, review, and utilization of data for programmatic decision-making. Work with MoH and partners to forecast and quantify health commodities based on annual national demand. Closely work with RHD, HTSS, CMST and relevant partners to develop distribution plans, monitor delivery schedules, and facilitate the timely delivery of commodities. Provide technical assistance to districts in monitoring stock levels, anticipating upcoming needs, ensuring appropriate storage conditions, and maintaining accurate records of all health commodities, including inventory levels, distribution, and consumption trends. Monitor stock levels, consumption trends, and pipeline data and support the developing and updating of the supply plan of health commodities to ensure continuous product availability at all service delivery points. Strengthen national planning through supporting the MoH to routinely collect, analyse and review data on commodity consumption through participation in the supply chain core group. The Supply Chain Associate will play a significant role in conceptualizing and developing supply chain dashboards where necessary for MoH utilization to facilitate ease of data visualization and programmatic decision-making. Support in designing additional supply chain tools where necessary to improve the use of data for decision-making, including design of data collection tools, leading data collection, managing and analysing data sets, and presentation of analyses to support decision-making. Support/coordinate trainings and mentorships for pharmacy personnel as required by closely working with MOH and district coordinators. Coordinate with district coordinators on the support provided to strengthen the district commodity tracking committees and drug therapeutic committees. Work with HTSS, RHD and other stakeholders to identify available resources, analyse funding gaps and mobilize resources to fund national plan. Perform any other relevant duties and lead day-to-day implementation of activities as assigned. Bachelor’s degree in relevant field required, such as Pharmacy, supply chain, logistics, Public Health, Nursing, Social Sciences; experience on supply chain management preferred. Minimum 10 years of relevant experience in a demanding, result-oriented environment in the public and/or private sector. Professional experience with a minimum of 4 years in supply chain management in the public sector or other relevant private and public sector experience. Proven experience in health commodity quantification, Logistics Management Information System (LMIS), and data analysis. Proficiency with supply chain management tools and software (e.g. QAT, GFPVAN). Excellent written and oral English communication skills. Demonstrated ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and tactfully to various audiences. Exceptional Microsoft Excel skills required, including experience using Excel for quantitative analysis or costing. Great ability to communicate effectively using PowerPoint and Word. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and quantitative skills, and ability to use data to inform program development and strategy and to present results in both narrative and graphic form. Proven ability to operate independently, multitask, and set and achieve ambitious targets with limited guidance. Advantages Master’s degree in Public Health, Global Health, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, or a related field. Demonstrated experience working with government ministries and partner organizations within the SRMNH sector. Experience supporting supply chain management systems for SRMNH commodities and supplies. #jobreference2 #region3

review_candidates.description: Job Description Approche Tiers Conformément à L'engagement Pris De Préserver Les Capacités Et De Soutenir Le Personnel Déjà En Poste Au Sein De L'Organisation, La Majorité Des Postes Vacants Au PNUD, Au FENU Et Au Programme VNU Sont Publiés Selon Un Processus De Candidature à Plusieurs Niveaux, Dans Le Cadre Duquel Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026 Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA) Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes Veuillez prendre note du ou des niveaux indiqués dans l'intitulé du poste vacant, le cas échéant, et vous assurer que vous remplissez les conditions requises pour postuler. Background Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est le réseau mondial de développement du système des Nations Unies. Présent dans de nombreux pays, il accompagne les États dans la recherche et la mise en œuvre de solutions adaptées aux défis nationaux et mondiaux en matière de développement. À travers son expertise, ses ressources et son réseau de partenaires, le PNUD contribue au renforcement des capacités nationales, à la promotion d’un développement inclusif et durable ainsi qu’à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Le Niger fait face à un ensemble de facteurs de fragilité interdépendants, notamment l’insécurité et les violences armées, les conflits communautaires, les déplacements forcés, les inégalités socio-économiques, la faiblesse des capacités institutionnelles et locales, l’accès inégal aux services publics essentiels, le chômage et la vulnérabilité des jeunes, l’exclusion de certains groupes sociaux, ainsi que les effets croissants du changement climatique. Ces facteurs se renforcent mutuellement et affectent particulièrement les régions exposées aux conflits et aux déplacements, notamment Tillabéri, Tahoua et Agadez. Ils compromettent la cohésion sociale, la confiance entre les populations et les institutions, les moyens d’existence et les perspectives de développement durable. Dans ce contexte, le PNUD Niger, en partenariat avec le Gouvernement du Niger, met en œuvre le projet « Renforcement de la Stabilité et du Relèvement Socio-économique dans les régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua et Agadez (2026-2030) ». Le projet constitue une intervention stratégique de stabilisation et de relèvement visant à agir de manière intégrée sur les facteurs de fragilité et à consolider les acquis des interventions antérieures du PNUD, notamment ceux issus du Mécanisme de stabilisation du Liptako-Gourma. Le projet s’inscrit dans le cadre du Programme Intégré Gouvernance (PIG-Niger), du Document de Programme Pays (CPD) du PNUD, du Cadre de coopération des Nations Unies pour le développement durable (UNSDCF), du Plan stratégique du PNUD et des priorités nationales, notamment le Programme pour la Refondation de la République et les orientations nationales en matière de gouvernance, de paix, de sécurité, de développement local et de résilience. L’intervention est structurée autour de trois résultats complémentaires : (i) le renforcement de la cohésion sociale, de la prévention des conflits, de la réconciliation communautaire et de la prévention de l’extrémisme violent ; (ii) l’amélioration de l’accès inclusif, équitable et sécurisé aux services publics et sociaux essentiels et le renforcement de la gouvernance locale ; et (iii) le renforcement du relèvement socio-économique et des moyens d’existence, avec une attention particulière aux femmes, aux jeunes, aux personnes déplacées internes, aux ex-associés aux groupes armés et aux autres groupes vulnérables. C’est dans cette optique que le bureau pays du PNUD au Niger recrute un/une Analyste de Projet et de Coordination Terrain, qui jouera un rôle clé dans la coordination des activités terrain, la liaison avec les partenaires et le renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux dans les régions ciblées. Le PNUD adopte une approche de portefeuille afin de s’adapter à l’évolution des besoins et de tirer parti des liens entre les interventions pour atteindre ses objectifs stratégiques. En conséquence, le personnel du PNUD est appelé à travailler de manière transversale entre unités, fonctions, équipes et projets, au sein d’équipes pluridisciplinaires favorisant la collaboration horizontale. Rôles et Responsabilités Sous la supervision du/de la Chef(fe) de l’Unité Stabilisation et en lien avec le Team Leader Gouvernance, Paix et Sécurité, l’Analyste de Projet et de Coordination Terrain assure la coordination opérationnelle des activités de projet sur le terrain, la liaison avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre, le renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux et la capitalisation des bonnes pratiques.
